Zakliczyn Jewish Military Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zakliczyn, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Zakliczyn dates to the 17th century, though the town's Jews had no cemetery of their own, burying their dead instead in Brzesko; the population reached 295 (25 percent) by 1921, most later murdered by the Germans at Bełżec in September 1942. Around 1915, the Austro-Hungarian Military Department of War Cemeteries established War Cemetery No. 293 here, designed by architect Robert Motka, as the burial site for soldiers of Jewish origin who died in WWI — 11 soldiers of the Austro-Hungarian Army and one of the Russian Army, all killed between January and June 1915. It is the only Jewish military cemetery in the Lesser Poland Voivodeship; in 2018, the Commune of Zakliczyn carried out renovation work using regional voivodeship funds, adding missing nameplates for the dead.
